stories.headline: DNI memo: Iranian plots against Americans have reached 'advanced stages'
stories.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio in an Oct. 23 memo that Iran has stepped up efforts to target US personnel, Reuters reported. The State Department has updated travel advisories for more than a dozen Gulf and Middle East countries.

stories.headline: San Juan River crests at record in Farmington; more rain could bring a second rise
stories.summary: The San Juan River crested at Farmington, N.M., above its 1909 record, after about 20 more overnight rescues in San Juan County. Power is out in Shiprock, evacuated areas remain closed, and officials warn rivers may rise again with more rain.

stories.headline: Energy Dept. lends up to 400,000 barrels of SPR crude to Louisiana refinery
stories.summary: The Energy Department authorized an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve's West Hackberry site to Phillips 66's Lake Charles refinery after a crude delivery disruption. The oil must be returned with premium barrels, which DOE says comes at no extra cost to taxpayers.

stories.headline: Illinois man gets 2 years for staging hundreds of fake robberies for U visa fraud
stories.summary: Parth Nayi, 29, of Woodridge, Ill., was sentenced to two years and fined $50,000 for organizing hundreds of staged armed robberies nationwide so fake victims could seek U visas. Participants paid him $5,000 to $30,000 each, prosecutors said.

stories.headline: Ukraine says Starlink back to full speed; Musk says Kyiv broke terms
stories.summary: Ukraine said Starlink and Starshield returned to pre-restriction speeds after more than a week of throttling that disrupted front-line drone operations. In his own posts on X, Elon Musk said civilian Starlink was never allowed for offensive drone strikes, and that Starshield, a separate system, is controlled by the US government.
stories.whyItMattersToUS: A US company's service to a US-backed ally was cut back, and Reuters reports the throttling order came from inside the White House.

firstHand.quote: Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be. Starshield, a different system, is controlled by the US government. What they decide to do is up to them.
Starlink's terms have remained consistent as a civilian system, not a means of killing. Violation of those terms will result in end of service. Starshield use is a decision of the US government.
